sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Core Philosophy**: GRIHA is based on the principle of 'what gets measured, gets managed', focusing on **Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)** of buildings.
• **Institutional Origin**: Developed by **TERI** and adopted by the **MNRE** as the national rating system for green buildings in India.
• **Scope**: It evaluates buildings on a **100-point scale** across various categories including site planning, water management, energy efficiency, and waste management.
• **Key Metric**: The **GRIHA Index** measures the environmental impact of a building from design and construction to operation and eventual demolition.

items.definition: A technique to assess environmental impacts associated with all stages of a building's life, from raw material extraction to disposal.
One of the 8 missions under NAPCC; GRIHA serves as the primary tool for achieving the mission's goal of energy-efficient urban planning.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Energy Efficiency**: Integration of ECBC (Energy Conservation Building Code) standards.
• **Water Management**: Mandatory rainwater harvesting and wastewater recycling protocols.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: High initial capital cost, lack of awareness among developers, and voluntary nature of the rating.
• **Solutions**: Incentivizing GRIHA-rated buildings through Floor Area Ratio (FAR) concessions and fast-track environmental clearances.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'GRIHA-SWEM'
• **Decoded Meaning**: S-Site Planning, W-Water Management, E-Energy Efficiency, M-Materials/Waste Management.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses GRIHA with LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design). Remember: GRIHA is indigenous to India, while LEED is an international standard (USGBC).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Climate-Responsive Architecture' when discussing GRIHA in the context of urban planning and the 'Urban Heat Island' effect.

keyTakeaways: GRIHA is the official national rating system of India for green buildings.
It is a voluntary, performance-based rating system aligned with the National Mission on Sustainable Habitat.
It emphasizes the entire life cycle of a building, not just the operational phase.
